messages:
maya: quick design q: when the rerank API returns scores for N candidates, should we expose a model-agnostic probability (0-1) only, the raw logit, or both? thinking about billing, console display, and downstream comparability.
alex: +1 to a normalized score for product/console. downstream devs expect 0..1. logits are useful but noisy across model families.
tj: agree but we should keep raw for diagnostics. suggest `score` (0..1) always + `debug.logit` present only when debug flag is set.
sarah: watch payload bloat. some customers send 5k candidates. debug logits by default will be painful. docs should recommend debug only for small batches.
emily: propose API shape: array of objects so we can attach ids and per-candidate meta: `[{"candidate_id":"c1","score":0.87,"meta":{}}]`. require `score` rounded to 3 decimals for wire; logit in `debug` with higher precision.
maya: rounding note: 3 decimals ok for routing and cost dashboards; full-precision for offline eval in debug.
ops-bot: canary deploy: rescorer-v4 -> canary by @deploy-bot at 2024-08-22T14:02:10Z :rocket:
alex: important for routing: affinity should try primary model_family, fallback to cheaper compatible variant. console needs to show when fallback happened and which model produced the scores.
tj: absolutely. never translate/fake-normalize a fallback model's score to look like the primary. include `produced_by` and `model_version` fields in response.
sarah: quota semantics: charge per-candidate-scored. unit = candidate_score_unit. each model_version has a `model_unit_multiplier` documented in console pricing page. quota calc example: `units = num_candidates * multiplier`. console should show cost per 1k candidate-scores for selected model.
emily: defaults: `max_candidates=500` (soft), `hard_limit=2000`. requests >2000 -> 413 with clear error. SDKs should expose chunking helpers.
maya: telemetry: capture a `score_histogram` (buckets: 0-.1, .1-.3, .3-.6, .6-.8, .8-1) per model_version + counts, plus p50/p95 latency and sample size. use this for regression alerts.
alex: add events: `rerank.request`, `rerank.candidate_scored` (per candidate), and `rerank.fallback` with tags: model_family, route, customer_tier.
tj: routing policy detail: route by `model_affinity` then by `cost_preference`. policy must be expressible in console as simple toggles: affinity-strict / affinity-preferred / cost-preferred.
emily: rollout UX: console playbook to run % canaries or customer-tag targeting (e.g., org:beta). telemetry-by-slice (canary vs baseline) should be automatic.
maya: backward compat: add `compat=legacy_list` query param that returns the old `scores: [..]` list for 3 months. prefer deprecation header and migration guide.
alex: response example we should standardize in spec:
```n[
  {"candidate_id":"c1","score":0.932,"meta":{},"produced_by":"rescore-v4-20240820"},
  {"candidate_id":"c2","score":0.121,"meta":{},"produced_by":"rescore-v4-20240820"}
]
```nplus optional top-level `debug` with `logits` array when debug=true.
sarah: perf note: for serving batching & KV-cache hit rates, recommend typical candidate sizes 50-200 for best throughput. include this in quickstart.
tj: tests: unit tests for envelope shape, compatibility mode, and an end-to-end check that fallback sets a `fallback=true` flag in logs. add load tests at 50/200/1000 candidates to measure cost & latency.
emily: I'll draft the console mockups and the migration doc. will include example quota math for clients and an SDK snippet showing auto-chunk.
maya: thanks all. @alex @tj please review when emily posts the doc.
ops-bot: deploy finished: rescorer-v4 -> canary at 2024-08-22T14:07:02Z :white_check_mark:
